lens: CLARITY & DEPTH: would a curious 15-year-old follow it and an expert respect it?
lensNote: The lens text names AlexNet and the transformer; this film is about Handwired, so I judged the brief's three deep dives in their place (ternary to ReLU, ch04; host loop and patterns, ch06; gradients, ch07). The 'beliefs, dissenters and how long they held' test uses the tag device: ch02, ch08, ch09 and ch11.
ledgerCheck: Round 1: qa/reviews/ held no earlier reviews and film.json stages.fixes was empty, so I had no fixed, partial or skipped ids to verify.

issues.problem: The document tape is drawn mirrored. In pass 2 ('from the start', 19:20-19:24) and in the top strip at 19:18.6 the glyphs are flipped ('ɘ', 'ƨ', 'ɿ'), so the highlighted 'error' reads 'ɿoɿɿɘ'. A viewer cannot read the JSON being searched, and that is the whole point of the two-pass beat.
issues.fix: Remove the horizontal flip from the tape glyphs. Show direction with the sliding motion and a small arrow, never by mirroring text. Pass 1 should move the reader window right to left over text that reads normally. Re-check the sheet at 19:16.7, 19:18.6, 19:20.5 and 19:24.1.

issues.problem: The step that explains 'bit reads two' is missing. The plate shows a = 16,777,222 · bit = 2 · 20-12 = 8, but never shows why: a-4 = 16,777,218 is exact, while a-5 = 16,777,217 has no float and rounds to 16,777,216 (the small red × at 16,777,217 is the only hint). A 15-year-old hears 'the second ramp's input rounds down' and sees nothing that rounds.
issues.fix: At the 'rounds' beat (7.20 s), ink two short lines under the ruler: 'a - 4 = 16,777,218 ✓' and 'a - 5 = 16,777,217 → 16,777,216 (no float there)', then 'bit = 218 - 216 = 2'. Animate the a-5 marker dropping from 217 into the 216 tick before the 'two' beat.

issues.problem: 'It magnifies by two to the hundred and forty-ninth' comes with no reason. The 16-operation comparison is the payoff of Deep Dive I, and the expert will want to know why it is exactly 2^149: the smallest positive float32 is 2^-149, so multiplying by 2^149 turns the faintest possible difference into 1. The lens strip (×2^14 · ×2^24 ×5 · ×2^15) appears with no explanation.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'Promise only a range, and it must tell the tiniest difference from none. The smallest float is two to the minus hundred and forty-nine, so it magnifies by two to the hundred and forty-ninth, in steps.' Then re-time ch04-s10 'lenses' to land on 'in steps'.

issues.problem: Deep Dive I loses its thread. After the 4.5 → 11 dimmer and the 2^24 failure, the film detours for about 60 s (ch04-s12 snap trick, ch04-s13 1,732 px window, ch04-s14 float64 study) and then cuts to 'The real library won't compare until you promise a range.' A first-time viewer no longer knows which comparison is meant. Each detour is good on its own; the missing piece is a bridge back.
issues.fix: Open L0414 with a bridge: 'Back to a greater than four. The real library won't compare until you promise a range.' Optionally show the README tag '(a > 4) ? 10 : 12' in the first second of ch04-s08 before the emitCompare error card.

issues.problem: Two lines are too dense and their connection is never stated. L0614 ('Handwired saves only at events and fixed checkpoints. Other frames replay from the last save, are drawn, and thrown away.') is a hard idea delivered in one breath, and L0615 ('Now a busy drag frame runs about seventeen') never says that the 17 runs are this replay. The viewer gets the tag strike in ch06-s05b without the reason.
issues.fix: Make the cause explicit: 'One run per frame? That held until mid-September. Replaying from the last save means a busy drag frame now runs about seventeen.' Consider splitting L0614 at 'Other frames…' so ch06-s05 'rehearsal' gets its own breath.

issues.problem: This silent 9 s plate shows an unexplained bug: '3·v vs v·3, slope at v=0 → 0 vs 3', 'both ramps on their corners', 'fixed that morning · 274 tests pass'. The narration never mentions it, so a 15-year-old cannot decode it, and an expert sees a claim with no context (why a multiply built from ramps has a word-order-dependent gradient at zero).
issues.fix: Either (a) give it a caption line set in the plate's hand, timed at 'corners': 'a multiply built from two ramps: at v = 0 both sit on their corners, so the slope depended on which side the zero was', or (b) ask story for one narrated line (route to the line owner), or (c) cut the shot and give its 9 s to ch08-s05. Never leave it silent and unexplained.

issues.problem: On L1206 ('Three beliefs are still argued over…') the frame is a wide of about 20 tags whose text is illegible at 1080p. The three named beliefs are never isolated, so the summary the whole film builds to cannot be read.
issues.fix: On each of the three names ('Learn the weights', 'Fully differentiable', 'regular JavaScript'), push in or lift that one tag forward with rim light and dim the rest, then pull back to the wide for L1207.

issues.problem: The 2020 dissent is anonymous and abstract ('one human neuron's branches answered either input but not both'). The film's own device asks 'who doubted it', and the bible names Gidon et al., Science, 3 Jan 2020, XOR-like.
issues.fix: 'In 2020, Albert Gidon and colleagues found one human neuron's branches answering either input but not both, an exclusive or: a job thought to need layers of gates.'

issues.problem: 'The longest chain of gates runs seventy-one deep' follows 'a hundred and thirty layers deep' with no link. Viewers will ask why the two numbers differ.
issues.fix: Add a clause: 'The loom is a hundred and thirty layers; the longest chain of gates, the part nothing can fold, runs seventy-one deep.'

issues.problem: 'Its steps one after another' does not tell a teenager why that makes a GPU slow. The ch05-s06 plate has the numbers (2.2 ms vs 81 µs vs ~140 µs) but no reason.
issues.fix: '…ran fifteen to twenty-seven times slower: a hundred and thirty layers, each a separate trip to the card, with too little work in each.' (The claim needs a check against the bible's GPU dispatch claim before narrating.)

issues.problem: The 1,732 px example says 'Doubles fit seven; thirty-two-bit floats fall a hair short' but never says what is being fitted. The formula f(f(1732-24) × f(1/244)) = 6.9999995 is on screen and goes by fast.
issues.fix: 'Fit columns two hundred and forty-four pixels wide in a window seventeen hundred and thirty-two wide. Doubles say seven; thirty-two-bit floats say six point nine nine nine, a hair short.'

issues.problem: The row-boundary labels read 40, 80, 80, 140, 180. The repeated 80 looks like a typo to a teenager and is never explained (a zero-height row?).
issues.fix: Use distinct boundaries (for example 40, 70, 85, 140, 180, still giving three yeses at pointer 90), or label the repeat 'empty row'.

issues.problem: Automated QA reports ghost text: the 'toggle · track 52 × 32 px' and rail labels overlap from 6.88 to 24.05 s. The same check flags ch06-s03 ('distance from home' over the loupe, 7.47-13.88 s).
issues.fix: Use the type kit's textSwapOut so that only one label layer stays above 25% at a time. Re-check ch06-s03 in the same pass.

issues.problem: The STT check fails: 'Lou' was heard as 'Lu' in L0301 and in L0810. The listening sign-off for Kleene, Cheng Lou, TOML and RegExp is still pending.
issues.fix: Add a lexicon alias for 'Lou' (as in 'low') and re-narrate L0301 and L0810, then run film:voice signoff for the four pending terms.

issues.problem: The film averages 151 wpm, but 21 lines run at or above 186 wpm. Several sit inside the deep dives where numbers arrive (L0401 192, L0405 195, L0423 191, L0604 199). In the densest arithmetic a 15-year-old needs a beat to land each number.
issues.fix: Add 0.3-0.5 s of air after the number-bearing clauses in L0404, L0405 and L0423, and slow L0604 and L0308 to under 180 wpm. Keep the overall runtime by trimming silent holds elsewhere (for example ch04-s16 or ch07-s12).

best_moments: ch04-s06: 4.5 worked fully on screen (0.5 × 10 + 0.5 × 12 = 5 + 6 = 11), then 4.25 → 2.5 + 9 = 11.5 on the 'dimmer' beat. It is exact, step by step, and the picture is in sync.
ch04-s05: the unchosen belt carries ∞ and the plate turns into 0 × ∞ = NaN. This is the clearest picture of why 'both branches always run' matters.
ch04-s12: 2^23 + 1 = 8,388,609; 0.49999997 → 0 and 0.5 → 8,388,609.5 → ties to even → 8,388,610 → 1. That is real IEEE-754 behaviour, shown one tick at a time.

ch07-s03 and ch07-s02: the valve y = 3w·max(0, g + b) with w = 0.5, g = 0.25, b = -0.1 gives 0.225, ∂y/∂w = 0.45 and ∂y/∂g = 1.5; lowering b to -0.4 shuts it and every slope goes to 0. Gradients are taught with checkable numbers.
ch06-s03: one 4 ms spring step (-300, 0) → (-296.88, 780) through a real 2×2 matrix, then M^300 by squaring: 14 operations for any step count.
ch06-s08: 799.300048828125 (in a row) vs 799.2999877929688 (in pairs), then 'drift: loop 5.67 px · tree 0.26 px'. Float grouping is made visible to the last digit.

ch04-s09: 'Who tied it on? The caller. Who doubted it? The validator. How long it held? While the input stayed honest.' This is the film's belief device working at the level of a single function call.

ch02: Sutton's Bitter Lesson and Brooks's reply six days later. ch09: the GPU tag that held for hours. ch11: the TOML rule written before the test. Each era has a believer, a dissenter and a duration.
